title: RES Pipeline Branch — Automated Manufacturing Workflows
description: Pipeline automation milestones for the RES track. These milestones close the loop from print to program, validate the pipeline with matched test cases, and convert 15,504 hardcoded programs into parametric macros. Depends on foundational harvesting (RES-MS0), NC pattern mining (RES-MS11), and tool database (RES-MS14).

milestones.title: Macro Conversion Engine — 15,504 Hardcoded → 8-12 Parametric Macros

smart_config.role: CNC Macro Programmer + Pattern Recognition Specialist

tribal: 97% of 15,504 lathe programs are hardcoded (absolute coordinates, no variables)
G85/G87 roughing-finishing pairs dominate 97% — Okuma OSP native cycles, NOT G71/G70
Die cavity types from Excel macro: MailBox, Altracs, Taptite, Heading Die, Squares
Q1.nc is the MODEL parametric macro: uses #variables for dimensions, G2 arcs with R#11
Structural fingerprinting reveals 8-12 macro families based on operation sequence patterns

reference: H:/PRISM/JM DIE/CNC OKUMA MULTUS/ (5 multi-axis programs)

milestones.intent: 15,504 hardcoded lathe programs collapse into 8-12 parametric macros. Instead of programming each new die from scratch (copy old program, manually change every coordinate), the machinist enters dimensions (#1=bore_diameter, #2=depth, #3=taper_angle, etc.) and the macro generates the full toolpath. Each macro family covers a die cavity type and operation pattern — Q1.nc style with #variables replacing hardcoded X/Z coordinates, G2/G3 arcs using R#N for radii, and G85/G87 cycles with parametric depth/feed. 15,504 files become 8-12 files plus a dimension lookup table.

U-MCR01.title: Build MacroFamilyClassifierEngine — fingerprint 15,504 programs into 8-12 structural families
U-MCR01.description: Analyze all 15,504 parsed programs (from RES-MS11's MinProgramParserEngine output) to identify structural families based on operation sequence fingerprints. A fingerprint is the ordered sequence of: (tool_type, operation_type, cycle_code) — e.g., [T0100:facing:G96, T0300:rough_bore:G85, T0300:finish_bore:G87, T0500:drill:G81, T0700:thread:G76]. Programs with identical fingerprints (same tool sequence, same operation types, same cycle codes) belong to the same macro family. Use hierarchical clustering: exact match first, then fuzzy match allowing ±1 tool variation. Map families to die cavity types (MailBox, Altracs, Taptite, Heading Die, Squares) where possible. Output: MacroFamilyCatalog with family_id, fingerprint, member_count, representative_programs[], die_type_mapping, parameter_dimensions[].
exit_criteria: 8-12 macro families identified via fingerprinting
Each family has >100 member programs (statistical significance)

U-MCR01.four_loop: BUILD → SCRUTINIZE (/prism-review) → GAP FILL (/test with real program fingerprints) → TIE UP (no TODOs)

U-MCR02.title: Build ParametricTemplateExtractorEngine — extract #variable templates from representative programs per family
U-MCR02.description: For each macro family, take the representative programs and identify which coordinates vary between members while the structure stays constant. These varying coordinates become #variables. Process: (1) Align programs within a family by operation sequence, (2) Identify constant vs variable coordinates (X, Z, R, F, S values), (3) Map variable coordinates to physical dimensions (bore_diameter→#1, depth→#2, taper_angle→#3, radius→#4, etc.), (4) Generate Q1.nc-style parametric template: replace hardcoded values with #N references, add G2/G3 arc parameterization (R#11 pattern from Q1.nc), parameterize G85/G87 cycle depths and feeds. Use Q1.nc as the gold standard template format. Output: ParametricTemplate per family with #variable list, dimension meaning, valid range per variable, and the template G-code.
exit_criteria: 8-12 parametric templates generated (one per family)
Each template uses #variables for all varying dimensions

Roundtrip validation: template + original dimensions = original program ±0.0001
U-MCR02.four_loop: BUILD → SCRUTINIZE (/physics-verify + /program-validate) → GAP FILL → TIE UP

U-MCR03.title: Build MacroConversionValidatorEngine — validate 15,504 programs reproduce from 8-12 macros + dimension tables
U-MCR03.description: Mass validation engine that proves the conversion is correct. For each of the 15,504 hardcoded programs: (1) Classify into macro family via fingerprint, (2) Extract dimensions from the hardcoded program, (3) Instantiate the family's parametric template with extracted dimensions, (4) Compare instantiated output vs original program line-by-line (allowing formatting differences), (5) Score: exact_match, coordinate_match (within ±0.0001), structural_match (same operations, different values). Report: conversion_coverage (% of programs successfully converted), accuracy (coordinate match %), outliers (programs that don't fit any family). Build a DimensionLookupTable per family: {program_name → [#1_value, #2_value, ..., #N_value]} so any historical program can be reproduced from macro + lookup.
exit_criteria: Conversion coverage >90% of 15,504 programs
Coordinate accuracy >99% for converted programs
Outlier analysis: every unconverted program has documented reason
